open_points.subject: trial case expected outputs
open_points.question: When expected outputs are present, must they contain exactly every contract output port, or may a case assert only a subset?
options: Require exactly all output ports
Allow a partial expected-output map
Allow expected outputs to be absent only, otherwise require all ports
open_points.default_guess: Require exactly all output ports when expected outputs are present.

open_points.subject: effect refusal trace
open_points.text: Record the owner's approval or refusal of a requested approval.
open_points.question: Where does effects.decide_effect_approval obtain the exact StoredValue and SpooledFile references required for the refused element's NodeExecution inputs, since its inputs contain only the approval identity and M24 names input digests and a preview?
options: Persist exact input references in EffectApproval
Pass the element inputs from runs when deciding
Have effects reconstruct the inputs from the run trace
open_points.default_guess: Persist the exact input references in EffectApproval and use them for the refusal record.

open_points.subject: trial file fixture inspection
open_points.text: a file — StoredValue fixture or SpooledFile — as digest, size and media type, its bytes only through read_spooled_file / read_spooled_file takes only a SpooledFile — never a StoredValue
open_points.question: How can the owner receive the bytes of a trial-case file fixture, as required by the rule that the owner receives every value, when the only byte-reading surface operation expressly excludes StoredValues?
options: Allow read_spooled_file to read file-carriage StoredValues too
Add a separate fixture-byte inspection operation
Define that file fixtures are never returned as bytes
open_points.default_guess: Extend the owner-only inspection read to accept file-carriage StoredValues.

open_points.subject: failed-run spool removal
open_points.text: A spool that cannot be removed then is removed at the next start / a spool that cannot be removed does not [stop the start] / Spools of ended runs that keep none are gone
open_points.question: What observable result and recovery behavior apply when spool deletion fails repeatedly, given that release and cancellation claim removal but neither the request nor the next start fails?
options: Fail and stop until deletion succeeds
Return success but record a durable cleanup failure and retry
Return success indefinitely while inaccessible bytes may remain
open_points.default_guess: Record the lifecycle change, report an internal error, stop, and require startup cleanup to succeed before serving.

open_points.subject: content-addressed bytes without records
open_points.text: The bytes exist in the content-addressed area. / When a request makes several store changes, those made before the failed one stay. / The only files the kernel keeps beyond a run are the file fixtures of trial cases.
open_points.question: What happens to bytes published by put_value_bytes when the following record_change fails, leaving no StoredValue, constant, case or run record that names them?
options: Stage bytes and publish them only with the naming record
Remove unreferenced bytes after the failure
Garbage-collect unreferenced bytes at startup
Keep unreferenced bytes permanently
open_points.default_guess: Stage the bytes and publish them only when the naming record is committed.

open_points.subject: repair-view continuation token
open_points.text: The continuation token is the store position of the last item returned / a continuation token that also carries the implementation set of its first page
open_points.question: Is a repair-view continuation token only a store position, or must it also encode a potentially unbounded implementation snapshot, and how does that fit bounded_text_bytes_max?
options: Encode the complete implementation set in the token
Store server-side paging state
Carry a snapshot boundary and reconstruct the implementation set
Do not snapshot the implementation set
open_points.default_guess: Carry the cursor and a snapshot store position, then reconstruct the eligible implementation set from durable records.

open_points.subject: resend after not_applied
open_points.text: sending one again after not_applied needs a fresh approval, as for every class / The one exception is a resend after an attempt resolved not_applied
open_points.question: Does the fresh-approval rule cover every EffectAttempt whose status is not_applied, including a direct 4xx and a later run of a draft-write, or only an unknown attempt that the owner resolves as not_applied within the same run?
options: Every later matching send across runs
Every resend within the same run
Only attempts resolved from unknown to not_applied
open_points.default_guess: Apply it only to an unknown attempt resolved not_applied within the same run, because that is the only resend path specified.

open_points.subject: store first-start behavior
open_points.text: Take the exclusive lock, check the data directory and remove temporary files before any record is read.
open_points.question: On a first installation, must open_store create a missing data directory, SQLite database and internal areas, or must the host pre-create them; and which missing items are a refusal versus an internal error?
options: Create the directory and all store structures
Require the private data directory but create its internal structures
Require every store structure to exist
open_points.default_guess: Require a pre-existing private data directory and create the database and internal subdirectories inside it.

open_points.subject: MCP listen address
open_points.text: The MCP entrance opens only after every start step.
open_points.question: When is the configured listen address bound, and what happens if it is invalid or already in use after recovery has changed records?
options: Bind before recovery but accept no requests until recovery finishes
Bind only after recovery and stop on bind failure
Treat listener setup as a host responsibility outside serve_kernel
open_points.default_guess: Bind after recovery; on failure, report a sanitized start error and exit non-zero without opening the surface.

open_points.subject: sandbox startup probe
open_points.text: Check at start that bubblewrap is present and one probe execution succeeds.
open_points.question: What exact code, inputs, bounds and assertions constitute the probe, and is it intended merely to run successfully or also to verify namespaces, network denial, traps, limits and cleanup?
options: A minimal successful function execution
A fixed release probe checking isolation and cleanup
A suite covering every sandbox restriction
open_points.default_guess: Use one fixed release-owned probe that verifies execution, isolation essentials and confirmed cleanup.

open_points.subject: installation loading checks
open_points.text: Load and check the configuration file at start. / Enforces A regular private file of the kernel's user, not a link; tokens of at least 43 characters, pairwise distinct.
open_points.question: What is the complete ordered set of load_installation checks, including parsing, required fields, unique agent names, credential header syntax and service identifiers, so that the first reported start failure is deterministic?
options: Apply every State 1 and State 2 installation constraint in one specified order
Limit load_installation to the checks listed in its Enforces section
Split remaining checks among later startup operations
open_points.default_guess: Check file safety, parse and required structure, unique agent names and tokens, then credential and service configuration, in that order.

open_points.subject: manifest JSON duplicate members
open_points.text: the service record is absent, is not valid JSON / record_digest is the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of that one capability entry
open_points.question: How is a manifest object with duplicate member names handled before canonicalization, since ordinary JSON parsers may silently keep the first or last member and JCS cannot represent duplicates?
options: Reject the manifest as invalid JSON
Reject it as a separate manifest mismatch
Accept the parser-selected member
open_points.default_guess: Reject the manifest as invalid JSON before any binding or digest is produced.

open_points.subject: service base URL composition
open_points.text: one that is not an absolute http or https URL with a host counts as none / The URL is the api_base_url without a trailing / followed by the declared path
open_points.question: Are query strings, fragments, user information and path components allowed in api_base_url, and exactly how are multiple trailing slashes and an existing base path joined to the operation path?
options: Require an origin-only base URL
Allow a base path but forbid query, fragment and user information
Allow every absolute URL and define an exact URL-join algorithm
open_points.default_guess: Allow a base path, forbid query, fragment and user information, remove trailing slashes deterministically, and append the declared path.

open_points.subject: masked failure_detail length
open_points.text: a failure_detail of an execution whose class is above open is returned to an agent only as its length and that class
open_points.question: Is the reported length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode scalar values or characters after truncation?
options: UTF-8 byte length
Unicode code-point count
Length of the original untruncated detail
open_points.default_guess: Return the UTF-8 byte length of the stored, bounded failure_detail.
